assertionOptions.description: WebAuthn PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions (opaque here) for the one assertion that proves possession of the passkey just registered: a fresh challenge of at least 128 bits, distinct from the creation challenge, single-use and bound to this registration, with the community's rpId. allowCredentials is omitted — the credential does not exist yet — and the installer's page sets it to the rawId navigator.credentials.create() returned.

options.description: WebAuthn PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions (opaque here). pubKeyCredParams lists exactly EdDSA (-8, Ed25519) and ES256 (-7, P-256), the two algorithms whose key the administrator's did:key can name; user.id, user.name and user.displayName name no DID.

registrationId.description: Echoes the install token's jti (a UUID); pass it back to vtc/install/claim/passkey/finish.

schema.description: Begin claiming a fresh community with a passkey: exchange the install token (and its claim code, when the token was issued with one) for a WebAuthn registration challenge, and the assertion challenge with which the installer will prove possession of the passkey. The passkey ceremony of vtc/install/claim/start 0.2, with the administrator's DID derived from the passkey's own key — Ed25519 or P-256 — and never named by the token. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

claimSecret.description:
A short code the operator receives **out of band**, alongside the install URL but through a separate channel.

The second factor on a claim: the URL alone is deliberately insufficient, so a stolen or forwarded install link cannot claim the passkey by itself. A maintainer that mints one shows the plaintext once and stores only a hash; a claim that omits or fails it is refused before any registration challenge is issued.

Optional in the schema because a maintainer may issue tokens without one — but a maintainer that does issue one MUST require it, and SHOULD issue one for any invite that travels over a channel it does not control.

installToken.description: The EdDSA-signed install JWT (aud=vtc-install) printed by vtc setup.
